title: External static reuse audit: PYNQ image resizer
conclusion: The frozen zynq-ps-pl-performance 1.0.0-rc1 workflow is useful as an evidence-organization and measurement-caveat framework for this unrelated PYNQ resizer, but this static-only packet does not validate hardware behavior or general PYNQ portability. A high-priority possible row-stride correctness issue requires confirmation before treating the saved timing as a valid baseline.
objective: Review supplied static image-resizer evidence for platform and interface identity, PS/PL dataflow, DMA contract, saved notebook timing meaning, source locations, and a minimal next check. Second round: explicitly review the same allowed source bundle using zynq-model-identity and zynq-dma-debugging workflows, while preserving the first-round selection history.

prohibited_actions_not_performed: No training, inference, Vivado, HLS, or C-simulation execution

selected_skill.name: zynq-ps-pl-performance
selected_skill.selection_rationale: The task is principally about PS/PL dataflow and what a saved timing measurement can support. Platform identity and DMA contract are reviewed as evidence within that performance workflow.
selected_skill.reuse_assessment: partial: useful for framing measured versus estimated results, separating dataflow timing components, and withholding FPS/P95 claims without evidence; detector-specific MAC/postprocessing assumptions need adaptation to pixels and image correctness. No blind or hardware behavior validation was performed.

source_identity.declared_design_target: The supplied Pynq-Z2 resizer Tcl names Vivado part xc7z020clg400-1 and instantiates processing_system7.
source_identity.overlay_identity: unverified: notebook expects resizer.bit, but supplied manifest has no .bit or .hwh file

findings.summary: The concrete Tcl targets xc7z020clg400-1 and uses processing_system7; the notebook loads resizer.bit, but no bit/HWH or runtime board evidence is supplied.

evidence.detail: Target part, IP catalog, Processing System and clock/HP0 configuration.
Overlay filename and Python IP object names.

findings.summary: Tcl wires DMA memory masters to PS HP0, GP0 to AXI-Lite controls, and streams through 4-byte/3-byte width converters around the 24-bit HLS resizer. Notebook uses contiguous uint8 RGB buffers and starts/waits both channels.

evidence.detail: DMA properties, width conversion, PS configuration, stream and memory/control interfaces.
Pixel and stream width, adapter behavior, TLAST/TKEEP, control and resize kernel.
Buffers, DMA transfer sequence and dimension registers.

findings.summary: The adapters use i*rows+j as a single Mat index. Under row-major linear indexing this overlaps row spans for the supplied non-square dimensions; exact vendor Mat semantics and behavior remain untested.
findings.integrity_note: No source modification or execution was performed. Treat as a candidate data-ordering defect pending confirmation, not as a demonstrated runtime failure.

findings.summary: Saved output is 1 loop, best of 3: 247 ms per loop; the timed body includes run_kernel and Image.fromarray, while setup and display are in other cells. It is not isolated PL latency, P50/P95, sustained FPS, or a reproducible current board baseline.

evidence.detail: Outside-timing setup and timed run_kernel implementation.
Separate initial invocation and display cell.

findings.summary: The checker looks for a success string in an external routed timing report. The report itself is absent, and the Tcl FCLK0 value is configuration rather than measured clock or proof of timing closure.

evidence.detail: External routed report scan and success/failure condition.
Configured PS FCLK0 value and HP0 enable.

frame_byte_alignment.note: Arithmetic only; not a transfer trace or TLAST/TKEEP validation.

linear_row_major_stride_check.assumption: Mat write/read argument is a zero-based row-major linear pixel index.
linear_row_major_stride_check.caveat: The vendor Mat implementation was not in the permitted input set and was not inspected.

next_minimal_check.action: Run an isolated, tiny non-square C-simulation of the exact HLS adapters using unique per-pixel RGB markers; confirm Mat index semantics, row/column order, frame byte counts, and TLAST/TKEEP boundaries before relying on the timing output.
next_minimal_check.reason: It is the smallest discriminating check for the i*rows+j suspicion and stream contract, without using the notebook or claiming a new board run.

Vendor xf::cv::Mat index implementation and adapter C-sim correctness
Cache synchronization behavior for cacheable buffers

zynq-dma-debugging.same_execution_evidence: No wall-clock timestamps, kernel session ID, DMA snapshots, or failure record; execution counts do not prove the output cells came from one current board run.

contract_review.data_length: Source passes whole arrays to sendchannel.transfer/recvchannel.transfer; computed shape byte counts are not actual transaction-length logs.
contract_review.stream_boundary: Input adapter sizes reads from dimensions and does not inspect incoming TLAST/TKEEP; output adapter asserts TLAST on final pixel and sets keep to all ones. No AXIS transaction trace exists.
contract_review.cache: cacheable=1 is present and explicit flush/invalidate is absent from the inspected notebook snippet; driver auto-sync behavior is unknown, so no cache fault is inferred.
contract_review.ownership_initialization: The function waits on both channels, but no status/error/length/state snapshots or initialization history are supplied; safe reuse/replay cannot be established from runtime state.

zynq-dma-debugging.incident_assessment: No actual DMA failure incident is captured. The workflow supports static contract review only; no DMA root cause or recovery decision is made.
zynq-dma-debugging.next_minimal_check: First perform the previously identified tiny non-square C-simulation of the exact adapters to check index and stream-boundary behavior. If a runtime failure is later investigated, capture one same-run transaction state before considering recovery; do not reset/replay without board-level contract.
